Another beautiful Casio watch with a drawback. The blue face and band make this an attractive watch. It has several great features, including the triple sensors (altimeter/barometer, compass, and thermometer), solar charging, Multiband 6 atomic time keeping, and Smart Access pull-out crown for setting functions. I have small wrists (5.5" circumference), the band fit well, and the case size was not too large for me. The silicone band is quite comfortable. The hands are "bold" and easy to read for the time, as is the smaller dial that indicates which function is active. The downside: The digital read-out window is of the "negative" type, meaning that it has lighter chararcters against a black background. It is nearly impossible to read unless you are in very good light and it is illuminated at the correct angle. Furthermore, the illuminator is not at all bright, so trying to see the LCD panel in the dark is practically impossible. Plus, the luminescent hands and numerals fade rather quickly in the dark. I have tried a few Casio watches with the negative LCD panel, and I have returned all of them. Now when I look at Casio's, I first look for analog/digital and then the type of LCD panel and stick with ones with dark characters against a light background. I suggest Casio ditch the negative LCD's. But that having been said, if you will not rely on the LCD panel very often or at all, this is an attractive watch with a load of convenient features, but many of them depend on being able to read the LCD panel. It can be done if the lighting is right, but it's not easy otherwise

So, I work way too many desk hours, and, while I am endeavoring to take more frequent breaks, and even bought a little stepper machine to use in my office, research on health led me to compression socks. given that I've got a bit of neuropathy setting in, which is not good. I was pretty surprised at the prices, and, of course, it's hard to know if the "knock off" brands are any better than "branded" brands. Since I knew nothing of compression socks, it's been a hit and miss of trial and error.

I wanted something white (not sure what's up with so many compression socks coming in wild color combos and designs?) and, starting out, I eventually found some great copper infused compression socks on here, by FuelMeFoot, that are 15-20mmHG which was a good beginning (and three pairs for ten bucks is awesome!). Then, hot weather hit, and it's very difficult to find a regular athletic or crew length sock to wear with shorts (wasn't really wanting to rock the lederhosen look, haha), but, finally found some from ADLU. Of course, a shorter compression sock doesn't do the same job, and I get that, but the ADLU are a nice balance of looking like "normal" socks plus providing some compression benefit and, at 15 dollars for two pairs, it's not that bad, since regular socks have gone up in price, yet seem to have gone down in quality at the same time.

But, having gotten used to (and actually really liking) how compression socks feel, I wanted to notch up to a more therapeutic level of compression, that I could wear while sleeping, at least a few nights a week, so I started exploring brands of those type. Read the many great reviews for these, but, with seeing much less expensive options, I tried those first, just because 20 bucks a pair is steep.

I ordered one of these, to compare, and, NO comparison, these are definitely the BEST of what I've found. The level of padding, and comfort, and excellence of fit is phenomenal. Extremely well made socks, and they just feel wonderful to wear. I know, kind of odd, socks that feel so great, but, seriously, these make my feet and legs very happy. I sleep great, and it seems my neuropathy is not getting any worse, and may even be starting to improve, so three cheers for compression socks, and a thousand cheers for these Wanderlust socks, the best of what I've found thus far, in a higher compression sock.

They even sent a coupon for my next order, and I just ordered two more pairs. They are thicker than the FuelMeFoot ones, so I'm not sure they will work as well in my sneakers, but, as an around-the-house and sleep-at-night sock, these are awesome. If they don't make my shoes fit too tight, I will likely switch over to these when the weather warms up, and possibly wear these exclusively, since they offer more therapeutic effect.

A terrific sock, and thanks to all the reviewers on here for sharing their findings. Wish I'd had these when I used to do overseas travel, but glad I've found them now!

The spacious interior is divided into three sections by a zippered center compartment. Despite it's reasonable size, this tote offers plenty of storage capacity.

Sure looks like the original. From any distance, this looks for all the world like a real Speedmaster. I thought that, surely, the maker of the real "Speedy", with its iconic and unique design, would be seeking what the lawyers call injunctive relief. The case size is 42mm diameter and 14mm thick with 20mm lug spacing. Black dial with long, thin, high-viz white hands and three sub dials at or below the dial's horizontal center line. And the tachymetre scale on the fixed bezel is the real deal, although I doubt many people will take the time to learn how to use it. (I didn't and probably won't learn how to use it, but I understand that it's used in conjunction with the chronograph seconds hand to measure the speed of an object or person over a predetermined distance. So, a time/speed/distance calculator familiar to any blue-water skipper. )
Closer inspection of the watch will reveal lots of differences. Inside the case is a Seiko quartz movement, not a multi-jewel Swiss mechanical chronograph. The bracelet, with solid end links, closely resembles the real Speedy bracelet, but it's obviously of somewhat lesser heft and quality, especially the clasp. I can't comment on the comfort of the bracelet, because I replaced it with a rubber strap right out of the box. And the three sub dials, there's the rub. Different sub dial functions on the Pagani vs the Speedy. So, not to worry, Speedmaster, this Pagani Design 1701 is an homage to your accuracy and stellar aerospace history, not a clumsy stylistic ripoff

Update 11/21/2016:

Shortly after above post the company reached out to me and shipped a replacement belt. Belt arrived and was in perfect condition. Quality control might be lacking at times but customer service is excellent. I did not expect anything in return and did not ask. I did not plan to return original belt. One might ask why... Well one question asked was if it was usable as a gun belt and figured I would give it a shot.

As a gun belt this is what I can say. In waist belt functions excellent. Thickness of belt combined with compression from body and versatile tension from buckle provides all that is needed even with a double stack full size pistol.

Outside belt is trickier. The thickness can support the weight of a full size gun but the width is going to give you some play. You will have to chose a holster made to be used with a standard belt. Smaller guns worked best because less tension was needed to remove from holster however the larger guns you could feel the belt shift while drawing unless you tightened the belt beyond reasonable.

Bottom line If the your looking for a nice belt I think you can count on this brand to deliver. If your looking for a nice dress belt for conceal carry this belt does work quite well IWC but OWC you will have to chose the gun and holster more carefully

Old School Charm. I didn't grow up in America, although I've lived here for 18 years now. But up until a week ago, I had never heard of Dopp Kits. It simply wasn't an expression that was ever on my radar. I've heard of toiletry bag, sponge bag, shaving kit, travel kit and so on. Dopp was simply not something I'd heard about. Ever.

Oddly enough I wasn't even looking for a Dopp Kit per se, to keep toiletries in. What I was looking for was a small inexpensive leather bag to hold emergency supplies for my many business trips. A medicine bag / first aid kit if you will. My old one was pretty basic, then I was using some cheap freebie with some sponsor logo on it. I figured I could do better.

I loved how flat this one folds to so that it can be stored in my smaller computer bag that is never checked luggage. And I was honestly blown away by the quality and old school charm of this thing. It really feels expensive and well made, even though it is priced at half what I would have expected to pay.

Clearly the whole Dopp history is cool, and the old school connections that people remember from previous generations. In an era where something like this would be purchased and be used for decades.

I ended up liking it so much I have already ordered a larger model for my actual toiletries to put in my checked luggage for my business trips. And I am excited to try using that, as all my previous toiletry bags have been the modern kind, the most recent a Tumi hanging option.

As for this Dopp Kit here are the Pros and Cons:

PROS:

- Amazing value for money, feels a lot more expensive than it is.
- Great supple leather feels and smells great.
- Fantastic vintage charm (and I'm not a classic car kind of guy, but still, this is classy and nice).
- Feels well made and not cheap or unreliable.
- When closed it has a very small footprint for travel.
- Feels like owning a piece of history.

CONS:

- It's a bit small this model. So you better be willing to pack light. If like me you travel a lot and intend to take things like an electric toothbrush, hair brush, tubs of hair product and so on, you will need a bigger option.
- In the old school way, it only has one zipper and that zipper has to slide around a couple of bends to open and close. I read another review that complained this was not as easy as some bag designs and that is true.
- I feel like the lining might have been more upscale.
- Would have been nice to have an internal zipper pocket.
- Would have been better if it had some little rubber feet so it didn't sit directly on a wet counter.

The bottom line here is I think this is awesome, love the aesthetic and personality of this piece and I am already a repeat customer. Time will tell how this holds up, but honestly at this price, I can always buy another if necessary

Better than being bald in winter. For transparency's sake, it seems prudent to admit that I am in no way a hat person. Actually, I kind of hate them. Always have. And I'm from Buffalo, NY, notorious winter capital of the Northeast, so imagine all the mornings my poor mother spent jamming knitwear on my head before I went out to wait for the schoolbus in the snow, shouting at me through the front window when I threw the hats into the yard, her voice lost to the relentless, driving wind. Later in life I'd decide headwear of any kind makes me look short (shut up; it's legit), and the cycle continued.

However, I shaved my head on a feminist whim a couple weeks ago, and I don't regret any part of it except not preparing for just. how. cold. my head would be. My hair must've been made out of fiberglass or something, because without it there for insulation I've been shivering like a chihuahua. A bald chihuahua. A week in and my lifetime hat boycott went down the drain (and probably got stuck in that clump of hair I mistakenly assumed wouldn't get caught just past the trap). Apparently proving your worth as a human being isn't dependent upon patriarchal beauty standards doesn't keep you warm.

Since I'm a hat n00b, I just searched for "knit hat." Obviously the results numbered in the zillions, so I just picked the first one that cost less than $15 and wasn't hideousâ€”two days later I was as warm and toasty as I'd been with a full head of cozy curls. In other words, this hat does its job. It's doing its job right now, actually, saving me from the scalp hypothermia I'd otherwise be battling in my 68-degree house. Honestly, I'm still not entirely sold on the concept. I got two additional knit caps in addition to this oneâ€”y'know, for varietyâ€”both from different companies, with different material and different linings, but the result is the same: my head is warm at the expense of its freedom. Eventually my scalp gets itchy and claustrophobic, likely due to a mix of my own neuroses and having very little hair to provide a buffer for my bare, never-been-exposed-to-anything-before skin. Maybe I'm just not used to wearing something on my head.

Either way, none of the hats are at fault. They're decent, hardworking hats. This one in particular has an excellent fleecy lining that feels like you're pulling a lamb onto your head, which feels a lot nicer than it sounds, I promise. The pattern on the knitted shell adds toughness in both look and feel, adding just enough flair to ensure you'll have a different hat than everyone else in the room without having the ugliest hat in the room. I can't speak on the other color options, but the charcoal grey I chose is the perfect dark dove shade to compliment my Goth Lite wardrobe.

My only issue is with the shape, which when worn creates two points on my head that look like a lowkey attempt at wearing a cat costume in public. Luckily it's roomy enough to allow for some reshaping at the back, but if you have a large skull you might want to carefully consider how concerned you are with people thinking you're storing a book under your hat

High-quality materials, unfortunate branding. Update, 11/15/2018: Now that there is finally a price for the item ($109 as of writing) I will revise my impressions a little. I think that this is a good bag for the price purely in terms of materials. The leather and waxed canvas feel really good. However, the large, ugly logo still ruins the aesthetic. For a bag so highly focused on style, I just can't see why they chose such a large and boring mass-market design to place so prominently on the beautiful leather flap. It's a real shame. However, if you can ignore the logo or place something over it, this is a decent choice for a carry bag. Not the best buy you will ever make, but priced reasonably for the materials.

I had been holding off on reviewing this bag in the hopes that Amazon will refresh their stock, and I can actually get an idea of the real-world cost (I received this at no cost as part of Amazon's Vine program, but I always review products based on value versus cost), but it has never shown as available or shown a price. That's a pity, but I will go ahead and put down my thoughts as they are.

The materials are certainly nice. It's a combination of heavy full-grain leather and oil-treated or waxed canvas. Good old-world stuff. However, it's a little harder to get a good idea of how the stitching will hold up over time. These days, especially with goods like this that are assembled in low-cost warehouses overseas, the quality and durability of the stitching are the major opportunities for failure. I will certainly update my review with observations of long-term use.

The other major fault is simply the branding. The logo is large and very visible, marring the otherwise classy look of the bag, on the outer flap. If the logo was more understated or at least classier looking it might not be an issue, but it's a very big mass-market design choice that just looks ugly. Given that a large part of the reason you buy a bag like this is for the look, it's regrettable that they didn't rethink this

Looks Can Be Deceiving. The description, the appealing photos, and story of this bracelet set my expectations quite high; too high, perhaps, since the product disappointed.

I found the packaging quite nice, perfect for gifting once the cellophane wrapper around the bracelet was removed (see photo). The bracelet itself looked well-made, though I did not understand why the logo was placed on the inside of the clasp, where it was hidden from view.

It took me several minutes to figure out the magnetic locking mechanism that secured the bracelet closed. Then, upon trying the bracelet on, it felt like a vice around my 8-inch wrist. To remove the bracelet, I again fiddled with the clasp for several minutes. Perhaps it loosens up a bit over time.

I laid out the bracelet and found the measurements were made including the clasp, which accounted for its snug fit (see photo). I could not account, however, for my difficulty utilizing the clasp, unless it had something to do with the arthritis in my hands.

I did a bit of online research about the manufacturer, and made a few interesting discoveries. Despite the use of a logo depicting a Native American and the photos of a young man making these leather goods by hand, the Casisto.J company is based in Hong Kong and manufactures in China. The Perfect Bra. First a disclosure: I'm a guy. I don't wear a bra. I don't have any experience from the good side, the wearing side. But I'm in love with a woman I've known for 35 years and I suppose she wore a bra long before she knew me. So my perspective is that I know what I like and I REALLY know what she likes.

In our decades together, this is the first time I can recall her ever exclaiming that SHE LOVES THIS BRA. She has related to me the experience of going to some kind of salon or something where a "wonderful sweet foreign woman" (I have no idea what that means) 'handled the girls' and fit me with the most amazing bra". That was interesting, but the effect wore off after a decade or so.

So when my queen found that same level of delight after finding a bra online sight unseen, well, that caught my attention. Honestly, I've never been discontent, but if she's happy, then I'm double-triple-... I don't know what comes after that. Anyway, I'm Over The Moon happy for her. She deserves to be happy.

So there's a hidden gem in the center that only she and I know about. Frankly, that's gilding the lilies. For me it's almost a distraction. But for her, she knows she has a hidden treasure in there, and that's pretty fun.

Best of all though. this bra has these wonderfully humanitarian wide straps. I feel so sad for her at the end of the day when she takes her bra off and there are deep sculpted troughs in her shoulders from her straps. But this bra has beautiful wide comfortable straps that truly seem to be on her side. It's like there are little cherubs who are holding things up and ensuring that her back and shoulders aren't punished by what's happing up front.

OK. I'm done reviewing a bra. We've been deeply in love since 1986 and I don't think I've ever put so much thought into foundation wear. Honestly, I'm very simple to please. More importantly, I need my queen to be pleased. She's over the moon happy with this bra, so how could I not love it?

I have an awesome pair of winter boots that are warm and water-proof but not very comfortable, and I have I feeling that, between the two, I will choose these 80% of the time. The inner flocking sheds really badly. When I take my feet out of the shoes, my socks are covered in brown fur. I am sure that over time the loose bits will wear out of them and it will improve, but I have only worn them about 5 times so far. That is the reason for 4 stars instead of 5. The upper seems to be high quality, and the soles have enough bounce to them to feel good walking, but I don't feel that the two are glued together very tightly.  These may be just one-season boots, and perhaps I will update that they are or aren't come spring.  Also, the soles don't have deep grippy grooves for slippery surfaces, so these are more for keeping warm in mostly dry conditions, and less for in ice and snow.  Lastly, I wear a 6.5 and euro size 37. These boots don't come in half sizes, but I went with the sixes because the chart said they were 37s, and I am glad that I did. I would usually size up if my half size weren't available, but I am an American living in Asia and have come to find that their shoes that are marked 6 when no 6.5 is offered are usually better than a 7, and these are Asian shoes. I hope my review helps someone!

The holes are actually shown once in the "LATEX PROP" photo, so it's not a complete wash of false advertising. But they are oddly placed, and as difficult to see out of as the nose holes are to breathe out of (there's no mouth hole here). Additionally, the mask fits more snugly than I'd have thought, because it looks quite large.

Without seeing the product photos compared to what I received, and knowing the latex scent will eventually fade, I'd have initially given this 3 stars. To be frank: while I'm not in love with it, the thing does look quite good when worn. And it's priced fairly. hole and run in one sock, socks are different lengths, very thin, but compression is OK. I use compression socks for my venous insufficiency and varicose veins. I use 20-30 mmHg nearly all the time, for a couple of decades now so I know what to expect and how they should feel. I replenish the socks often as they are not meant to last forever (the sock may hold up but the compression decreases over time). SO I am always on the look out for a decent compression sock. These are NOT IT. I will tell you why:

The compression on these is about right. No real complaint there. Very important to select a size based not only on your foot size, but also on your calf size. If deciding between the two, I would aim for calf size or go to a different brand.

The positives: the ties seem well-constructed. They are a little narrower than I'm used to but not so much that I wouldn't wear them. Being 100% polyester they feel a bit coarser than silk ties but they can be machine washed, too, which may be a benefit to some people. There is a second cloth tab on the back that sports the manufacturer's name and serves as a second loop for tucking the tail of the tie. The tie length will be fine for most people who don't require an extra long tie. The negatives: if you like the feel of silk ties then you won't be happy with this fabric. And, for me, though I don't wear the most conservative ties, the silvery glitter makes the pink tie unsuitable for my work environment. For someone who likes a little more flair and/or for a special occasion, though, it will be an attention-grabber.

All-in-all it's a nice starter set and a nice gift set as well if the colors fit to the wearer's use. Right now the ties aren't available on Amazon so I can't see the current pricing but if they're in your price range and you are okay with the colors and the material, I think these are a good option

Had one similar from a major outdoor retailer till it got washed this one is as good for less!. These style hats have a metal wire in the outer brim that holds the shape (spreading brim out) to block the sun. I had the one from a major retail for several years with issue. Got it when family went to Cozumel and needed solid sun and rain protection headgear. When we got back it became my yard work hat and continued to impress. Till some deiced to wash and dry it. This caused the metal wire to bend and due to fatigue break. Hat was still wearable but due to where break was it was no longer working to prevent sun exposure. I mention all this to say that the YZKKE one I am reviewing has impressed me as much as the major retailor on did at 1/5 the cost.

Same wired brim to insure protection from sun and rain. The other hat claimed to the "cool comfort" and I cannot say that it achieved that but the YZKKE hat maintains the same "cool comfort" as the major retailer. The YZKKE has the option to be a Boonie (Australian) style due to placement of snaps on either side. I have not cared to use them but there presence is not a detraction from comfort or use so that maybe a personal preference. A note about the button/snaps, they are made to look aged brass and may be but they have some steel or similar "rusting" metal inside. I say this since around the edge of each of them you can see definitive rust discoloration so it may be that over time the snaps rust off or fall apart. As I do not use them I do not worry about a short term issue but expect someday they will rust out and fall off and that will be the end of this hat.

Revisiting the wired brim, the description of rolling the hat up for storage needs to be done in a way that works with the desired shape, meaning don't roll front to back unless you want the front to stand up straight from being rolled backwards. Instead if you are going to roll it up go from one side to the other and do not try to make it a super tight roll, unless you plan to remember and roll the other direction next time. As to washing, I have taken to washing it in the shower with me after being in the yard all day then hanging it up to dry. We recently moved from a washer with an agitator to one without, but I prefer not to risk it anyway.

Summary, great hat, super value, many features of expensive outdoor retailer, and may rust at snaps. I decided not to take a star off for the snaps rusting but will if issue become a problem in a short time frame.

Here are some observations as a relatively new user of period panties overall:

- It seems weird at first, but you really can just throw them in the washing machine (cold cycle) with other clothes and they come out clean. I have tested period panties with just a white shirt before and everything came out clean. Some people rinse them out first in the sink or shower before machine washing, but it's not totally necessary to do so.

- Plan time to air dry. They need about 12 hours. So you'll need multiple pairs.

- They really do absorb well and not leak. So far I have had zero leaking issues with all my thinx panties. I've used different styles for all levels of flow (light to medium-heavy). No leaks to speak of! I love that they give peace of mind.

-They are comfortable. I feel like they give the protection of winged pads without the irritation of the plastic wings.

- I still use tampons and pads on really heavy days. Mostly this is a comfort thing... I think the thinx panties would work just fine, but I don't enjoy the feeling of pulling them back on when I've used the restroom and they are starting to get saturated. I prefer the feel of changing to a fresh pad or using tampons on those days. The moisture wicking works well, but you can still feel that it's not completely clean and fresh when you're pulling them back on after restroom breaks.

- You have to remember to bring the next pair with you when you're ready to change them. I probably just need to keep a little box for clean ones ready to use near my toilet during that time of the month.

Overall I highly recommend thinx. I like that I can reduce my pad and tampon usage (less plastic, less chemicals near that part of my body). They are comfortable and don't leak

Score! The best readers I've ever found. These glasses are such a relief! It's hard to find readers in this strength (3.75), even harder to find metal frames, almost impossible to find an attractive design, and after all that they're always too big to stay on my face. These glasses are everything I wanted in terms of strength (of both prescription and construction), size, and design, in addition to being wonderfully clear, scratch resistant, and amazingly affordable. I'm extremely pleased with these glasses and (shhh, come closer so they don't hear me) I would have happily paid twenty or more for ONE pair -- getting four feels like riches! I'm narcoleptic with seizure disorder and my glasses get destroyed within days or weeks (bent, twisted, lenses popped out, but safer than the sharp edges of snapped plastic frames) -- I certainly can't afford prescription ones at my current rate of destruction. I read a lot and do detail work like sewing and wood finishing and jewelry repair, so I'm delighted to have found these. They come with protective plastic sleeves on the arms inside individual ziplock bags inside individual drawstring fabric bags inside a cardboard box inside Amazon packaging. The box is fairly cheesy but the drawstring bags are made of the same thick soft fabric as the two included cleaning cloths, they're not the thin black nylon ones that don't clean and do scratch. The prescription strength is on a little sticker on one lens and is not printed inside the arm, which is the only thing I would add to these -- if you have different strengths lying around you might want to mark them in some way to avoid confusion. I am going off my normal course somewhat and considering the advice from a previous reviewer, I did my own research into Bamboo fiber production. I did find similar information with regards to dangerous chemicals used in processing bamboo into soft fabric - the FTC website states soft bamboo textiles are processed into rayon using toxic chemicals.

I also discovered during my trek across the textile world, that soft bamboo is not the only textile that is processed using various toxic chemicals but also includes most man made fabrics! Leaving only a few natural fibers such as cotton, silk, linen, etc "safe". Yikes! Based on what I've read I'm really not sure why we are all still walking around.

With above caveat, my husband loves these socks and actually told me they were the most comfortable socks he has ever worn. Not sure how they will launder, he won't take them off! They are indeed extremely soft to the touch and well made.

So should you chose to keep the above Bamboo textile caveats in mind, I leave it up to each individual to decide for themselves with regards to these socks. Husband loves them!

Overall I love this little watch and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to friends

It's easy to drape around my shoulders and adjust unlike sweaters that seem to generate static electricity when I pull my arms through the sleeves.  The collar and front sides of this shawl have an attractive ribbing that keeps my neck warm - a bit like a scarf.  The fabric is limp so the collar does not stand up on its own.  The front around the neck/collar ribbing falls to a point on the chest.  I'm 5'3" and on me, the bottom point of the neck/collar ribbing is about at my waist.  The front of this shawl also ends in vertical ribs on the bottom 5 inches which hang at a slant.  On me, the bottom points of the shawl on each side come to just below my knees.  The back of this shawl drops to about mid-thigh on me.  Besides wearing this as a basic shawl, it's easy to toss one of the front ends over a shoulder although perhaps best to clip some way to keep it in place.  I'm sure there are other ways to drape this shawl as desired.  The instructions state that this shawl is hand washed in cold water and then laid flat to dry. Some of the best pantyhose I've owned. I am 5'6" and 170 lbs (size 12), and the 1XL fit me just right.  Being in my early 50's, I have been around since pantyhose were "de rigeur," so I've had a lot of experience in wearing them.  And I hate them.  The two biggest issues are that they bag at the ankles, or ride down in the crotch area.  Secondary issues are being too tight in the waist (making them uncomfortable and giving a funny muffin top), not being sheer enough, having noticeable lines running through them (cheap looking), feeling a little rough instead of silky, or just generally looking cheap.  Used to be, you could buy hose that looked good, but then have to constantly deal with baggy ankles, or buy utilitarian ones that were more durable--and looked it.  These hose are the best I've worn at being very sheer and silky, while still clinging tightly to my legs over time.  The waist is a little tight, but better than most.  (Tip:  make a 1/2" cut at the waistline to make a tight waist a lot more comfortable.  Only recommended with "control top" pantyhose.)  These appear to be control top panty hose, since they are not sheer to the waist, but I would rate the "control" as minimal.  The plus side of that is that they are more comfortable and easy to pull up than typical control top hose.  I wore them for about 5-6 hours and had no bagging in the ankles.  At 5'6", I had ample length in the legs to pull it up properly in the crotch area.  It did sag a bit over time, but much better than other hose.  I wavered between giving 4 or 5 stars, because their only drawback is that they do snag very easily, though it is a "black line" horizontal snag, and not the vertical "run" in hose that is a lot thicker and more obvious.  Over the course of wearing them, I got 3-4 snags.  All things considered, these are my favorite hose, and it's not a big deal at all having to wear them on the rare occasions that require them nowadays

Perfect for Wyoming Winters!. First off, I'm a woman with larger hands so it's difficult to find decent gloves that both fit my hands and that are also stylish ('cause let's be honest, it's always nice for gloves to not only do their job but look good doing it). Well, I stumbled across these and decided to give 'em a go. Man am I glad I did!

They were delivered quickly which was very much appreciated given a heavy storm.. perfect timing. That storm presented me with the opportunity to put them to the test immediately.

I purchased the large and they fit my larger hands, well.. like a glove. I couldn't ask for a better fit. I usually get gloves that are either 1) too small (most gloves I try) where the stitching for the web between my fingers is at least an inch above my actual web so I find myself always pushing them down which causes the stitching to give out prematurely.. or 2) too large (whenever I wear my husband's gloves) where the stitching comes down to my web but the fingers are too long and I have at least an inch (usually closer to two inches) sticking out beyond the tips of my fingers which causes me to drop anything I might try to pickup. Needless to say, finding the perfect gloves has been a long, seemingly endless battle for me.

But these gloves! Oh yes! They fit! They are so soft inside and out and the color is a nice neutral color that goes with practically anything. The stitching meets my web, there is no excess material extending past my finger tips and they are lined with some of the softest fleece I've ever felt.

Back to the storm.. I wore these gloves while we bucked about a 1/2 cord of firewood. It was cold (14F, 3F with wind chill) and wet as the wood pile had snow from a previous storm on it and it was beginning to snow again. So these gloves kept my hands comfortably warm.. even after they became visibly soaked. Since they are not specifically described as waterproof, I wasn't sure how they'd hold up to the wet snow but they ended up drying out and, other than being a little dirty, looked like they just came out of the packaging.

Their stitching is impressive. There are no uncomfortable bumps or lumps that some gloves tend to have along the fingers or fingertips and the stitching around the thumb and in the palm area is very well done and appears it will survive what I need to ask of them.

Bottom line... I highly recommend these gloves! I do believe they will withstand our infamously harsh Wyoming Winters, so they should be good for you too!

I ordered this dress in both the Purple color and Orange color in Size Large. I am 64 years old, 5' 6" and weigh 166. I was pleasantly surprised both dresses fit perfectly. I generally wear a size 12 (misses) in TJ Maxx-priced dresses. I am "pear" shaped and this dress does NOT accent my larger waist and hips. In fact, it is surprisingly flattering because it skims the problem areas. The "smocked elastic" hits me right under the bust, as it should, and as shown on the model. This is an empire waist but does not look like a maternity dress like many empire waisted dresses do. I do not feel dumpy in this maxi like I do in most!
The "Purple" dress is a patchwork print with many, many different, lovely colors and patterns. It has lots of blue shades, some lavender and corals. The predominant color is not purple on my dress. I really love the print. The buttons and elastic button loops are a light peach color.
Buyer Beware: The bodice of this dress is not going to fit if you are larger than a 36 B or small C cup because this dress will gap at the bust. The fabric fits like silk and does not have any stretch. It does have a one inch placket of fabric behind the buttons and that camouflages any really tiny gaps.
The short sleeves fit with ample room on my rather large upper arms.
Some reviewers mentioned a "puff" on the sleeve which is true and very noticeable on the Orange dress but not on the Purple dress. It just depends on how the gathers in the sleeves were sewn at the factory. I do not like the "puff" so I'm returning the Orange dress.
This dress is 100% Rayon, very soft and, YES, it will be wrinkled when you get it. It had a slight odor. Just let it air out and press it. I do not recommend washing or drying this dress regardless of the "washing instructions" because it is just too delicate and apparently will shrink (based on many reviews). The elastic loops for the buttons seem delicate as well so don't pull too hard. The cord tassel at the empire waist (not a drawstring) adds to the "boho" look and I liked it, contrary to other reviewers. Yes, Lots of buttons but I can get the dress on and off over my head by just unbuttoning 7 buttons.
Length: I am just under 5' 6" and the length is just perfect! The dress does not drag the floor on me and covers my legs. Fun poseable necklace holds shapes well; snake face looks goofy; metal has a smell to it. I saw this and immediately knew it was this metal poseable rope style necklace. If you have never had one, they are really fun. It's a thick piece of metal and instead of hanging and flowing like a chain, you pose it. You can make twists, or shapes, or just wrap it around your neck or arm. This necklace is just what I thought it would be for the poseable fun factor, but the metal has a smell, and it's not the best quality. It's not terrible and seems sturdy enough, but it's also cheapy cheap and the smell off the metal and the fact that the snake has a goofy face are not my favorite things.

First off, this style of poseable necklace is awesome. It's fun to play with. If you are hanging out, different people can play with it and put it on. My kids seem interested in it. Basically, you bend the metal rope of a necklace into shape, and the pieces are hinged to where they will stay posed. And, as far as I know, it will never wear out. I had a roommate with a similar necklace, and it just stayed poseable through lots or posing and reposing. If you know what I mean, then you know what I mean, and if you don't know what I mean, then you should strongly consider this necklace for the fun factor.

The look: The look is very much like product pics, with the exception that the model wearing it on her neck has perhaps been photoshopped or posed with two necklaces or they photoshopped bits of necklace onto a stock photo and miscalculated a little. The snake wrapped around my neck is quite a bit shorter, and I have a small neck. The visual impression is the similar, but there will be a little less tail and neck of the snake to pose. I have gotten good deals at vintage clothing stores before due to being able to buy unusually small necklaces which are a harder sell when people go to try them on. You will be able to get a nice coil with the snake tail and head if you wear it in a necklace like the product pic, but they will have to be closer to your neck and not so far down your chest. Total length of the snake necklace I got is just over 36 inches long when I was promised 35, so I got longer than promised - that's good for me - or might indicate some variation in length, who knows? I would say that the product pics do this justice, and you can basically get similar looks.

Quality: Not the worst, but not good either: The bendy poseable parts work and the whole thing stays together. This doesn't feel like it's going to break. But, it also is not quality - not at all. The metal has a smell to it. That's a bummer. And the snake has a goofy face. And the way the snake head attaches to the necklace looks choppy and doesn't flow. The way the snake head is attached is not aesthetic at all. I feel that if they had just put a plain cap on each end, it would be an improvement over goofy snake. But the product pics show that goofy snake, so I can't really fault it. The snake's eyes are glued in place, not set with metal brads, and I'm pretty sure they are plastic.

Price: This is thirteen dollars right now. I think it's fair. These poseable rope style necklaces are unusual and tend to be around twenty dollars in stores (and possibly also tend to be thicker when I've seen them in stores), so actually the price is fine. Poseable bendy necklaces are a gimmicy costume jewelry thing, so I don't know that a high end one will ever be an option. I do notice that this same exact goofy face snake style is available from several different drop shippers, and can be anywhere between seven and twenty dollars from different sellers here on Amazon.

Overall, it's poseable and I can twist or bend it and it holds the shape. It's an unusal type of chain/necklace and exactly what I was expecting. I'm happy with it. Love to play with it like a fidget toy, and it's basically what I expected from looking at the pics online

Excellent print quality; looks just like product pics; I believe it to be real silk. This scarf has bright colors, matches the images shown in product pics, and seems to be real silk from appearance and touch. I'm happy with it for my wardrobe.

Colors: I got the "Color 1" pattern, which is a reproduction of a close up of a Monet waterlilies painting with blue colors in it. Colors match the product pics and basically it looks as expected. One thing that I hadn't done as well to visualize is the solid color border. For this pattern, it's a plain cream border. I think it blended into the background of pics for me, so I didn't realize as much that it was there. My tastes are more bohemian and maybe if I had visualized better, I would have done a pattern with a bright border. But that's me visualizing, and not the scarf. The quality of the print is also really good. It's kind of a blotchy pattern, so I don't know that the pattern has a lot of detail, but the printing is good resolution. There aren't any pixelated or choppy parts and it looks nice in person.

Construction: The edges are folded over twice and then chain stitched. The fold is very tiny. Basically it makes it to where there isn't any exposed fabric at the edges. It's also to where if stitching were to start coming loose later, it's easy to mend with needle and thread and have the mending blend right in with the original. There's not much sewing in a big flat scarf, but the sewing that is here is pitch perfect.

Is it silk?: This is a satin weave. There's no place for me to cut a bit off and do a burn test without messing the scarf up, and I don't want to mess it up. Based on my past experience with silk, I believe that it's genuine. It feels like silk, has more of pearly luster than a shine, and drapes like silk. All packaging was labeled "100% silk".

Is silk worth it?: I actually have some cheap rayon scarfs and some expensive polyester scarves (Made in Italy polyester) with the crazy colors and light weight fabric, and I really like them. But it's a numbers game in terms of I bought those in person, where I could see and feel the fabric first. The sheen and drape are different for silk versus for imitation. I think it's a numbers game and silk is more likely to be good if you can't check it out in person first. I also tend to hand wash the synthetic scarves, because each is so sheer and they are delicates, so silk isn't more work.

Washing: Silk is made of proteins, so normal laundry detergent, which is enzyme based, will damage the fibers. Woolite is fine for soap (wool is also made of proteins). Quilting forums say that baby shampoo is also OK for silk, and that's what I use. I basically wash silk in a bucket by itself, swish it around with soap, then rinse, then hang dry. So far silk bedding I have has lasted much longer than you would think for fabric so thin and sheer. So, that's one possible way to wash this scarf.

Price: For real silk, I really don't think you will get a much better deal than this. I think the price is perfectly reasonable. (Right now it's twenty six dollars, just in case the price changes drastically after I write the review.)

Overall, this looks very nice in person. It looks every bit as good as the product pics. The print quality and the texture of the fabric are great. I can't definitively test if it's silk without damaging it, but I believe it to be silk from touch. If you like one of the patterns available here and are looking to try out a silk scarf as an accessory, then I think this is a good option

Gorgeous hose! Necessary, even though fashion says otherwise.. Sometime when I wasn't watching, people stopped wearing pantyhose with dresses and skirts, even to work or church. Personally, I like wearing nylons, especially in the winter, where even a teeny little layer adds some warmth. At the same time that pantyhose disappeared, so did the slip. (slip: a slippery garment worn under a skirt that makes it hang properly, and hides legs and whatever if the skirt fabric is at all see through) After insisting that every skirt or dress hangs better when coupled with a slip, I gave up and only buy those garments for myself.

These pantyhose fit beautifully. I prefer to purchase hose in a size that is bigger than my dress size, simply because I don't like to fight with them as I put them on. These are a bit bigger than I am, and I don't have to struggle. There are no weird wrinkles around the ankles or knees, and the waist fits beautifully. The hose are stretchy enough that even if you bought them in your dress size, I believe they would fit just as well.

As far a durability is concerned, I think that is entirely up to the end user. I have friends and relatives who get a dozen wearings of one pair of pantyhose, but I have never had more than two wearings of a pair of hose in my life. (Except for a scary pair of maternity pantyhose, which is best forgotten) These lasted my usual one wearing, and didn't fall apart before I got home, so I am more than satisfied.

Oh yes, wearing these make your legs look wonderful. Added to any suit, dress or skirt (with a slip, of course), your legs will look thinner and your whole ensemble will look put together, not just thrown on. If you work in any field that has you contact customers in a suit, for example, you need hose. These are a good pair, and I recommend them

Super cute dress (mint green w/ large white flowers). I ordered this dress in the mint green w/ large white flowers, and in the 'multicolor 2' black dress with purple and dark pink small flowers. The two dresses are really different, even though both are the same size. The 5 stars is for the green dress. I would give the black one a 3. (*The specific differences between the two are listed below)

The overall effect of the differences is that the black one seems like something a southern republican grade school teacher would have worn in the early 90s (I seem to recall a few outfits like this from my elementary days), while the green one has a timeless, artsy, bohemian vibe. I do think the black one can be styled in ways that are cool & modern (despite its inherently uncool look), but the green one is ACTUALLY cool & very pretty.

I'm keeping the black one to use as a 'beater' dress for events where I want to wear a flowy dress but don't want to care if it gets dirty or even ruined--sitting on grass/sand/rocks/etc., walking in mud & wet grass at festivals/outdoor parties, sitting around smoky campfires, frolicking at the edge of the sea, etc. (all of which are more fun in a flowy dress--especially one that you don't mind messing up!) But the green one is perfect for more 'civilized' things like... pretty much anything else where you'd want to wear a pretty long flowy dress... but especially brunch. This is basically a perfect brunch dress. If you like brunch, get this dress, is what I'm saying.

Also, some people said that the lighter colors were see through but the mint green one isn't-- when I first tried it on I had navy blue shorts underneath and you couldn't see them at all. I'll probably wear a skin-colored bra & underwear to go in public, but I was afraid that it would be much more sheer than it is. (However, you can probably see an outline of your body if there is a bright light behind you).

Lastly, the only thing that would make this dress better (the green one anyway) is POCKETS. Why oh why aren't there any pockets in this???? You wouldn't even see them and it would be so convenient.

*The differences are: 1) the green sleeves are cut & sewed in a way that is more subtle & nondescript, the black sleeves are very very poofy; 2) the green one is a bit shorter, especially in the front & back (more of an asymmetrical hem that is longer at the sides), whereas the black one is floor length all around; 3) the green one is lower cut at the top, showing a hint of cleavage, and the black one is higher cut; 4) the black one has a string tied on the front that makes a long bow with tassels at the end, the green one does not have this. Also obviously the colors and patterns are different

Very Good Quality For The Price - Decent Materials, Good Construction. Y'know, for the money...? I think this is a really great hat. I've had nicer hats, but they cost literally 3 to 4 times more, and they ultimately didn't last me all that long anyways since I seem to just destroy hats quickly. I think because I'm really tall, they get snagged up in branches and stuff quickly. As such, I asked myself "why spend more on a hat that I'm probably gonna destroy or lose in a year, when I can just buy several less-expensive hats?" Well, this is that hat.

The materials are pretty decent. It's not really water resistant, but it'll keep rain out of your face. The mesh will allow good airflow, but keep bugs out. So far, after half a season, I see no evidence of deterioration due to HEAVY UV exposure. The material absorbs sweat fair enough, and can be gently hand washed clean. So far, it's held up to being snagged in three branches, and survived my storage compartment in my SUV. For the money, I think the materials are pretty good.

I was impressed at the build quality, for such an inexpensive hat. The stitching was clean and straight, without any loose threads. All the components were assembled well, leading to a perfectly symmetrical hats (one of my more expensive hats can't say that).

For the money, I got a hat that should probably have cost 2x more. Honestly, I think it even rivals a hat I have that cost nearly 3x more, as far as build quality. It's not as rugged as my even-more-expensive hats, but it doesn't have to - it's as good as I need it to be, and for a lot less money. My only problem is that it's just a little small. It sits a little higher on top of my ginormous pumpkin head than I would like, but so do my other hats. I just have an abnormally large dome - that's a me problem, not the fault of the manufacturer (I assume). It oughtta fit perfectly for most everyone else. Good hat for the money... I recommend it

From someone that loves watches...I really love this one!. This is simply one awesome watch! The PRW-6600 series from ProTrek is extremely user friendly. It packs a ton of features for an incredible price. What I love most about this watch is it's atomic timekeeping feature. A signal containing the precise time, day and date, measured by an atomic clock accurate to one second every 100,000 years, is sent directly to the watch using standard radio waves. I live in the US on the east coast and it has no problem receiving the radio signal. If you change timezones...simply pull out the crown and change it to the city within that time zone and this watch will automatically adjust to that timezone. Majority of the issues from previous Protrek models have been fixed with the 6600 series. This watch is also extremely comfortable.  I own a couple quartz movement watches and it is a tiny bit annoying when the battery dies. You could simply take it somewhere and have a jeweler change out the battery or do it yourself...but it usually takes me months before I find the "time" to do that. Aside from owning a couple automatic watches, this watch is solar powered which means this watch will outlive any other battery operated watch on the market.  The pictures I attached do not do it justice. It has great loom and the digital display has been easy for me to read despite some of the negative comments regarding that. But seriously, this watch is all analog! So anyone having issues with the digital display...you honestly don't need it.  My only gripe about this watch is that the dial window is mineral glass and not sapphire crystal. But for the price I honestly cannot complain. Truth be told...I love this watch. It's basically a smart watch that doesn't need to be plugged into a charger every few hours. No you can't make any personal calls or say, "Hey, Google." But for anyone that loves a watch with soul and practical functionality, this watch has something for everyone (i.e. World Time, Stop Watch, multiple alarms, timer, compass)

As good as any low-cost breathables. These are clearly inexpensive waders, and I'll be using them as a backup for the ones I favor. Some notes - they're made of the same or similar materials as most common breathable waders. Inside looks normal for breathables. The exterior is a little bit shinier nylon than I've seen in other waders, but they seem of average durability. The seams are sewn on the outside and taped on the inside. Most basic features are included. Booties are standard neoprene with soles a bit thicker than sides and taped seams. Integrated gravel guards are standard as well. Wading belt is standard and of typically low quality, as are the plastic buckles. Shoulder straps are elastic and standard. There is NO chest cinch on this model. There is one chest pocket with a waterproof/water-resistant zipper. The zipper is bright orange, which may scare fish! I do like the darker color of the material for camouflage.

The waders are lacking reinforcement at typical stress points like knees, seat and crotch. Seam joints also lack reinforcement on the interior.

Fit is a bit odd. I'm 5'10", 200 lbs and got a Large based on other comments. The waders fit well in the chest. waist and crotch. The legs are a bit long and therefore are quite baggy at the knees. The booties are HUGE! My feet are generally 8.5-9, US or 42 European. These booties would easily fit size 11-12 shoes, and my feet are swimming in them. That will create the potential for uncomfortable and perhaps leaky compressed folds inside my wading boots. More on that after I actually use these onstream.

All in all, these are probably worth around $50-75 US. I wouldn't spend much more than that. Great backup or travel version, especially if you're packing into your fishing location, or good for beginners and kids as an inexpensive starter set. You'll need to purchase wading boots as well - these are stocking-foot waders

Antiqued But Not Padded. This is a handsome canvas messenger bag with antique-looking distressed leather accents.

In person, the canvas has a bit more of a blue tint than the way it appears on my computer screen -- an online shades of blue guide suggests a color called "Air Force."

As others have noted, the buckled straps on the front are held shut by four magnetic closures which are easy to open and close, but not as easy as velcro, as you must align the magnets for closure.

A brass zipper with a leather pull tab seals a pocket on the back of the bag, useful for books or documents.

Inside, under the flap, one finds another sturdy brass zipper with a leather pull that secures the main compartment.

The main compartment is divided into three vertical sections, one of which is sealed by a nylon zipper with a brass pull.

One of the side sections has pockets for two pens and two phones or calculators. The side section opposite has a pocket sealed by another nylon zipper with a brass pull. This would be the place for your stash!

Unfortunately, none of these sections really has much if any padding, so if you wanted to carry a small laptop or large tablet in the bag, you would probably want to insert that in a padded sleeve.

The shoulder strap is removable, attached by brass clasps. I have deducted one star because although the product description says the strap is "padded," it lacks the cushioned shoulder pad that really adds comfort when toting such a bag.

The bag does get bonus points for its nice leather hand strap, however, and all the brass fittings seem to be well made and sturdy.

Finally, the bag comes enclosed in a lightweight canvas tote bag that might be useful for shopping or beach duties.

As I write this review, Amazon has not listed a price, so I can't say if the bag offers good value for the money or not.

What I can say is it's a good-looking bag with a number of useful features, lacking only padding inside and on the shoulder strap

Detailed Description of the Dress with Tricks!. I got this dress as a gift (since it was on my Amazon Xmas list). I purchased an XL since I do have a slightly bigger booty and wanted to make sure it covered it up nicely without any worry. So here are a few things about this dress...1. The material under the lace is WHITE, not nude. Some of the pictures lead you to believe it is a skin-tone material. It is bright white. Now, this may or may not be a big deal to you. It was concerning at first, since I have a medium-light Asian skin tone, but it looked really nice. 2. There is NO WAY you can wear a bra with this. Not even the ones that criss-cross on your lower back. The sides are pure lace. No material. So if you actually look at many bras, you will see the straps actually go along the side diagonally towards the lower end of your back. You will see these straps! You can try to wear the clear bra straps but I still think you will be able to see it. I would suggest YouTube-ing (I really hate to say this...) Kim Kardashian's no-bra boob taping video or other ways. Of course this is for us larger breasted women. 3. Since some people complained about the button falling off the top part of the dress (the area below the back of your neck), I would suggest sewing it on with a little bit of string to make it more sturdy. This way you won't have to worry about being out at night and the button falls off and then the back of your dress falling all weird on your back. 4. The zipper is very sturdy and visible. You can see this in the pics. It would have been nicer if they would have made the zipper black to match the dress vs. bright gold OR put a piece of fabric to cover the zipper in general, but for the $20 price, you can't be too judgemental. 5. The lace is really nice. I read that some people said there are a lot of unfinished lace on the ends...this is the way it's supposed to look. It's actually quite cute and gives it more of a flirty look. I would suggest using a starch spray to harden the lace (on the back) a little. just so the material looks a little more "pressed". Plus it'll help the look of how the overall material falls/lays on your back. Just be careful on the setting of your iron! Not too hot!  6. The skirt material is surprisingly nice. It is NOT "poofed" out like it shows in the picture. You can look on other reviewer's pictures and it lays flat. However, it is still a nice material. If you want a "poofier" look, I would suggest maybe finding a single layer tulle skirt to put underneath. It will give the skirt a little dimension (maybe even make your waist look a little smaller) and this will also help from keeping the dress going in-between your legs as you walk. It'll give the dress a more unified look as you are moving about. 7. Depending on how large your breasts are will depend on how much cleavage you will be showing. If you are showing a little bit of cleavage, YouTube how to contour your breasts with powder. It's amazing what a little bronzer can do! I hope this review helps for any buyers that are hesitant to purchase this dress. It is super cute and worth the $20

Functional... Well made... agravating (unless you are backpacking I guess). So I got this garbage bag... errr... poncho to try out. I'm a fairly large guy who doesn't fit well into the typical cheaper ponchos. We have a bunch of them that we take on our trips to WDW because the weather is so fickle in Florida. You never know when drenching rain will occur. When I saw this poncho, I thought it might be a good fit for my frame; I was wrong.

The poncho was nicely folded into the reversible pocket. The material is high quality. At first the poncho appeared large enough... until I put it on. First off, the buttons which hold the sides together kept coming apart every time I moved around. If you had a backpack, you would naturally need to unbutton them to fit it over the pack. However, I was intending to use the poncho while not wearing a backpack, so the constant struggle to keep the sides closed wasn't ideal. The second issue is the hand straps. While they should keep the wind from pulling the poncho away from your arms, the material barely came past my elbow. My forearms were mostly exposed to the outside and thus would get very wet. Lastly, the hood was a struggle to get on. At first I thought it was an elastic type opening but quickly realized it wasn't when trying to fit it over my noggin. I quickly found the Velcro release to make the hole wider but still couldn't fit it on... my wife noticed there was also a zipper near the Velcro which allowed the head to open up further. Now that I know how it works, it doesn't seem all that complicated, but had I waited until I was in the middle of a thunderstorm, I would have been soaked before I figured it all out. Minor annoyance though... but still didn't make a good first impression.

Overall this isn't a bad poncho. The material alone is much better than anything you will find cheaper in a local store (or the high priced ones you will find in a Disney store while seeking shelter from the rain). However it really does look like you are wearing a large garbage bag... which is not the image I want to portray to other people while I walk through a Disney park with my family. If you are a hiker, this might be a good poncho for you

So in sum, I'd say these fit me as an extra large, very closely.  I normally would expect to wear a LARGE in western sizing, so X-large is OK, but I would prefer my shirts to be just a bit larger. That little "feature" has caught the eye of others and resulted in my socks being complimented more than once now!

I am not a sock person at all -- I have peripheral neuropathy and my feet are a bloody mess. I cannot stand my toes being closed in (sometimes even shoes bother me and I have to wear open toed) but there are times when yoga socks don't cut it, you need an actual sock. I was looking for something that would be thin enough to not hurt my touchy feet but robust enough to not wear thru with use. And so when I was offered the opportunity to try these at promotional pricing in exchange for an honest review, I figured why not get something cute?

And they *are* cute. Really cute. I think the kitties are my favorite but I'm not sure. The colors are somewhat muted and sedate, despite the playful look of the socks. The little critters on your heel just put them right over the top for me though -- that's just so cute and I honestly have never seen anyone else do this. I've bought scads of printed socks for my daughters over the years, and even ones with little faces on the toes like this, but I have never seen heel critters before.

They're lightweight enough to not make your feet sweat heavily during a power walk, but sturdy enough to not rub and wear thru. They don't add too much bulk to most shoes. They fit snugly but not tightly, and they do not leave indentations in my ankles after wearing them. The way they're designed, you can pull them up tautly and they'll hit just above your ankle, or you can let them slouch a little and they'll rest right at ankle height. I like to let them slouch a little, it just looks cute with the stripes.

They launder beautifully. I machine washed two pairs in warm water with a cool water rinse. I air dried one pair and tossed the other in the dryer with the rest of the load -- I noticed no difference in how they fit afterwards, so I'm calling them safe to toss in the dryer.

Basing my opinion on the current Amazon price for these socks, I would say they are absolutely worth it. They are well made, fit nicely, launder well, and there is not one thing I don't like about them. The current price works out to just a little over two bucks a pair, and they're easily worth that. I definitely recommend them!

All function with just enough form to have become an enduring, timeless classic timepiece. For the right kind of person, with just exactly the right sort of style (or appropriate lack thereof), the Casio F91W is every bit as good as, if not better than, a Cartier. Th F91W is a classic. It's remained virtually unchanged for decades, and there's a reason for that. Certainly, it has its own look. It's slim, sleek, and sports the cleanest of clean lines. It's simple, and it doesn't make a big fuss. It's comfortable, it's accurate, and it does enough. Its alarm is positively reliable, and its stopwatch is simple and consistent. It's small and unassuming, and doesn't draw a lot of attention to itself because it doesn't need to. This watch exists for its wearer and no one else. It doesn't try to impress, but it will never let you down. It does a few things and it does them well, all the while, not pretending to care at all about the things it doesn't do.

It's a perfect watch for a woman or a man, for a child or an adult. It's good for sport, and it's good for relaxing, and it's good for work, and it's just fine for everything else in between.

If this watch were a person, when asked the time, it would reply "quarter to three!" with a big grin on its face, and go back to its drink without missing a beat. It wouldn't huff and fumble for the time and act as if you were intruding on it before somehow giving you a time that was an hour too fast or slow.

But you knew that already, didn't you? It used to be that you could find an F91W accidentally, just out shopping in the department stores. And maybe you'd need a new watch so you'd pick one up. But today, and especially online, the F91W doesn't really find you as much as you go looking for it. You wouldn't be looking at it if you didn't already know it was perfect for you. And if it's not the watch for you, that's fine too, just move along to something else. The F91W isn't bothered. It knows who its people are

Cuter than expected - size up if you want more length. When I first opened the package and felt the material I was disappointed and thought I would hate the outfit. The material felt like cheap costume fabric. It was not scratchy or gross feeling. Just thin and cheap feeling but still soft and smooth. However, when I put it on the fit was very nearly exactly what I wanted and it looked really great on so I am inclined to forgive the cheap thin fabric. Though it is important to keep in mind that as thin as it is it may end up being see through in bright light so if you are concerned test that and plan to wear something under depending on what you are wearing it for.

As for the fit follow the seller's size chart and look at their photos. It is true to what they list for the fit they show in their images (ie very fitted body con and really short). I don't prefer extreme fit body con or really short and cropped so I sized up by one based on what their chart said and it worked perfectly for me or almost perfectly. The skirt is just a bit above knee length and the top while still cropped is only mildly cropped and nearly reaches the top of the skirt. With a thin camisole underneath the top this should work out well.

For reference I am 5 feet tall and 110 lbs. Chest 32DD and waist is 26 inches. I have a short torso even for my height and longer legs so keep in mind if you have a longer torso this top will be more cropped on you. I ordered the size Large and it was almost perfect. I would have liked between 1/3 - 3/4 inch longer on the top and the skirt I would have been happy with another 1/3 of an inch or so. Everything fit a little looser then in the photo since I sized up but not in a sloppy or oversized way. Just in a nice comfortable fit kind of way. I would try another size up to get that extra length I really want but I am concerned that it would then be too loose on. If you don't mind doing lots of returns and want extra length you could always try both one size up and two sizes up and find out which you prefer otherwise just do one size up unless you are much taller with a longer torso

It looks super cute up. The hood is also rounded in the back so it doesn't come to a weird point like some other cheaper style hooded jackets I've seen on Amazon. The material is that of a sweater and will definelty pill with wear especially where your purse hangs or a seatbelt rubs. After just trying it on I had snags of fabric pull off with one of my finger nails so don't expect this jacket to hold up to daily use. But as a fashion piece to wear occasionally it is great and very unique. It also runs large. I plan on taking it in at the bust and waist. For reference I am 5'5 118lbs 34-25-38 meaurements and ordered a small. It is definelty a little too big in the bust and waist for my liking but because the lining isn't attached it's an easy item to take in on my sewing machine.
